config.documentTitleFull: BUSINESS SCREENING SERVICE DISPUTE FOR CORRECTION OR DELETION OF CRIMINAL HISTORY RECORD INFORMATION (10 M.R.S. § 1500-CC)

primaryStatutoryAuthority.description: Where the completeness or accuracy of a record is disputed by its subject, the business screening service shall investigate without charge; must review and consider all relevant information the subject submits and determine whether its record accurately reflects the official record maintained by the State Bureau of Identification; must correct a record that does not accurately reflect the official record; and if the disputed record is found to be sealed or the subject of a pardon, shall promptly delete the record. Within thirty days of receiving notice of the dispute the service must notify the subject of the results.

A business screening service is a person regularly engaged in the business of collecting, assembling, evaluating or disseminating criminal history record information about specific individuals for a fee, excluding a government entity and the news media.

A service disseminating records collected on or after 1 July 2010 must include the collection date and a notice that the information may include records that have been sealed or otherwise become inaccessible since.

verificationStatute.description: The dispute letter is the participant's own signed communication to a private company; the source records no notarization requirement and no verification statute. The participant signs and dates the letter personally; LegalEase never signs it.

counselFlags: This letter is correspondence to a private business screening service, not a court pleading, and the packet must describe it that way. There is no court, no caption, no service of process and nothing is filed anywhere.
Offer this route as a post-relief step attached to the sealing and pardon tracks, not as a standalone entry point. Do not promise deletion timelines.

Do not count this supporting action as substantive court record relief: chapter 239 binds business screening services only and reaches neither the State Bureau of Identification record (corrected under 16 M.R.S. § 709) nor the court record.

A copy of the sealing order or the pardon is required before sending, because § 1500-CC(2) makes prompt deletion mandatory only where the disputed record is found to be sealed or the subject of a pardon.
The packet neither pleads, demands, threatens nor calculates the § 1500-EE(3) statutory remedy ($1,000 or actual damages, costs, attorney's fees); that is litigation and outside self-help.
Whether a given entity meets the 'business screening service' definition in § 1500-AA is a participant question that may need attorney review; government entities and the news media are excluded.

Verification: the source records that the participant signs the letter and that notarization is none, and states no verification statute; verificationStatute.citation is left null and the letter carries an ordinary signature and date block the sender completes personally.
The vendor's dispute address is published by the vendor and varies; where the participant cannot find it the field stays blank with instructions to obtain it, never guessed.
Chapter 239 (10 M.R.S. §§ 1500-AA through 1500-EE) was enacted by PL 2025, c. 513, § 1 and is effective 29 July 2026; confirm effective-date posture at send time.

Attorney handoff triggers: vendor non-response after thirty days of receipt; a frivolousness determination the participant disputes; any interest in damages; any parallel Fair Credit Reporting Act claim; a dispute about accuracy where the record was never sealed and the true record must be established.

correspondence.subjectLine: Dispute for correction or deletion of criminal history record information under 10 M.R.S. § 1500-CC — background-check report dated {reportDate}
bodyParagraphs: My name is {senderName}, and I am the subject of Maine criminal history record information that your company reported. I dispute the completeness and accuracy of that record under 10 M.R.S. § 1500-CC and request its correction or deletion. My date of birth, for identity matching, is: [SENDER COMPLETES — DATE OF BIRTH].
The disputed entry appears on your background-check report dated {reportDate}. {reportReference} The entry reads as follows, exactly as your report printed it: {recordAsReported}
The correct status of this record is: {correctStatus}

Under 10 M.R.S. § 1500-CC, on receiving this dispute you are required to investigate without charge; to review and consider all relevant information I submit; to determine whether your record accurately reflects the official record maintained by the State Bureau of Identification; to correct any record that does not accurately reflect that official record; and, if the disputed record is found to be sealed or the subject of a pardon, to promptly delete the record.

Under 10 M.R.S. § 1500-CC, within thirty days of receiving notice of this dispute you must notify me of the results of your investigation, including whether the investigation was completed or terminated and which records were corrected or deleted. Please send your response to my mailing address shown above.
enclosures: Copy of the court's written sealing order, or of the pardon (copy only — the sender keeps the original)
Copy of the sender's official Maine criminal history record from the State Bureau of Identification (enclosed where the dispute concerns accuracy as well as sealed or pardoned status)
[ANY OTHER RELEVANT INFORMATION THE SENDER CHOOSES TO ENCLOSE — COPIES ONLY]
